configuration-not-read-intro: The target's package.json holds configuration this run could not use. Each line below says what this run did with its entry, and every account in this report is the one the target gives without it.
configuration-wrong-kind: {entry} is {is} where {reads} is read, so this run read it as absent.
configuration-unknown-key: {key} is not a key the specController block reads, so this run read nothing from it.
runner-key-not-a-layer: {key} — not a layer: the runner block is keyed by the four layers, and this key excludes nothing.
not-checks-entry-matches-no-step: {key} entry {entry} matches no step of the workflows this run read, so it makes no step a non-check.
not-checks-entry-not-a-step-name: {key} entry {entry} does not name a step as `<workflow file>:<job id>:<step name>`, so it makes no step a non-check.
proofs-never-ran: {count, plural, one {{count} Evidence Observation never ran to a result, so the behaviour it proves was never exercised.} other {{count} Evidence Observations never ran to a result, so the behaviours they prove were never exercised.}}
scenario-code-error-count: {count, plural, one {{count} scenario code error} other {{count} scenario code errors}}
no-feature-file-judged: No feature file was judged, so no scenario code is vouched for.
clean-no-coded-scenario: Scenario codes are clean over {featureFiles, plural, one {{featureFiles} feature file} other {{featureFiles} feature files}} carrying 0 feature codes (a feature code is the tag heading a feature file, the `<FFF>` that each `@SCN-<FFF>-<NNN>` code in that file repeats): no scenario in {featureFiles, plural, one {it} other {them}} carries an @SCN code to misfile.
clean-each-file-own-code: Scenario codes are clean over {featureFiles, plural, one {{featureFiles} feature file} other {{featureFiles} feature files}} carrying {featureCodes, plural, one {{featureCodes} feature code} other {{featureCodes} feature codes}} (a feature code is the tag heading a feature file, the `<FFF>` that each `@SCN-<FFF>-<NNN>` code in that file repeats): each file carries a code of its own, and every coded scenario sits in the file its code names.
clean-others-no-feature-code: Scenario codes are clean over {featureFiles, plural, one {{featureFiles} feature file} other {{featureFiles} feature files}} carrying {featureCodes, plural, one {{featureCodes} feature code} other {{featureCodes} feature codes}} (a feature code is the tag heading a feature file, the `<FFF>` that each `@SCN-<FFF>-<NNN>` code in that file repeats): each code is carried by exactly one file, every coded scenario sits in the file its code names, and the other {noFeatureCode} {noFeatureCode, plural, one {holds} other {hold}} no coded scenario.
unnamed-claim-ci-steps: {count, plural, one {{count} CI step} other {{count} CI steps}}
unnamed-claim-ci-steps-named: {count, plural, one {{count} CI step} other {{count} CI steps}}: {list}
scenario-code-errors-framing: {count} — each misfiles a scenario code, so the by-feature cut below cannot be trusted, and the run fails (exit 1). Every account still reconciles as it would if the code were filed correctly.
several-scn-codes-framing: {count} — each is a scenario carrying more than one scenario code, so no account was raised for it under any of them, and the run fails (exit 1).
misfiled-and-several-scn-codes-framing: {count} — each either misfiles a scenario code, so the by-feature cut below cannot be trusted, or is a scenario carrying more than one scenario code, so no account was raised for it under any of them. The run fails (exit 1).
duplicate-scn-code-not-listed: A duplicated @SCN code is not listed here: it is reported on its account's rows, as "{outcome}".
duplicate-feature-code: the feature code @{code} is carried by {fileCount} feature files — {files}. A feature code names exactly one feature file: a reconciliation's by-feature cut groups on it, so two files sharing a code report as one row and attribute one file's scenarios to the other. Give one of them a code of its own.
foreign-scn-code-carried: {file} carries the feature code @{featureCode}, but holds the scenario @{scnId}, whose feature part names {named}. A reconciliation's by-feature cut groups on the id, so it counts this scenario under {carrierCount, plural, one {{carriers}'s row, not {file}'s. Re-code the scenario for @{featureCode}, or move it to {carriers}.} other {the one row for {named}, which {carrierCount} feature files carry — {carriers} — so that row cannot say which of them it belongs to. Re-code the scenario for @{featureCode}, or move it once a single file carries {named}.}}
foreign-scn-code-no-carrier: {file} carries the feature code @{featureCode}, but holds the scenario @{scnId}, whose feature part names {named}. A reconciliation's by-feature cut groups on the id, so it opens a row for {named}, which no feature file carries as its header code, so that row stands for no file. Re-code the scenario for @{featureCode}.
no-feature-code: {file} carries no feature code, but its scenarios carry @SCN codes. A feature file is the class its scenarios' codes are filed under: give it a header code of its own, and code its scenarios for it.
several-scn-codes: {file}'s scenario "{scenario}" carries {codeCount} @SCN codes — {codes}. A scenario is one account, so it raises its evidence obligations under none of them, and a test citing any of them cites a code no scenario carries. Give it one code.
run-unsound: **This run is unsound.** {proofs} A broken proof sits on the row of the claim it names, as every Evidence Observation does. On a scenario's row, an Evidence Obligation of its kind of quality check that no other proof answers reads "Evidence Observation is missing", though its test may already be written. A broken proof on the row of a phantom claim or of the unnamed claim may be the proof behind any item of its kind of quality check that reads "Evidence Observation is missing", on any row. Fix what stopped each proof listed below from running, such as its test, the code it loads, its step definitions, its runner or the CI job that runs it. Then run them again and regenerate this report.
scenario-code-errors-gloss: the corpus files a scenario code under the wrong feature, so the by-feature grouping cannot be trusted. Read `{heading}` above.{alsoOutOfBalance} This run FAILED.
several-scn-codes-gloss: a scenario in the corpus carries more than one scenario code, so no account was raised for it under any of them. Read `{heading}` above.{alsoOutOfBalance} This run FAILED.
misfiled-and-several-scn-codes-gloss: the corpus files a scenario code under the wrong feature, so the by-feature grouping cannot be trusted, and a scenario in it carries more than one scenario code, so no account was raised for it under any of them. Read `{heading}` above.{alsoOutOfBalance} This run FAILED.
also-out-of-balance: The accounts do not agree either: at least one Claim Reconciliation carries a reconciling item.
out-of-balance-gloss: the accounts do not agree. At least one Claim Reconciliation carries a reconciling item. This run FAILED.
unsound-gloss: the evidence could not be TRUSTED to reconcile. A proof never ran, so the behaviour it proves was never exercised. Read the run-integrity stamp above before any count below it.
pending-gloss: every Claim Reconciliation balances, but Pending Items are outstanding and this run treats a deferral as a failure (`--strict`). This run FAILED.
balanced-gloss: every Claim Reconciliation balances: every Evidence Observation satisfies its Evidence Obligation.
nothing-to-reconcile-gloss: there were no accounts to agree. The ledger carries no Claim Reconciliation at all, so this run has NO BASIS FOR A VERDICT — the corpus `{corpusDir}` carried no scenario and nothing was produced. Not balanced: a run that examined nothing must not certify.
pending-items-outstanding: Pending Items are outstanding — deferred, not out-of-balance, so the verdict stands. A run that treats a deferral as a failure gives exit 3 under `--strict`.
reconciliation-totals-claim-reconciliati: A Claim Reconciliation is one row of the ledger: one claim, reconciled in its Quality Check Reconciliations. A Quality Check Reconciliation reconciles the evidence of one kind of quality check within the claim: the claim's Evidence Obligation of that kind, when it has one, against its Evidence Observations of that kind. A claim is a scenario, a phantom claim (a code that evidence cites and no scenario carries, which the table below calls an unknown Scenario) or the unnamed claim (the one row for the evidence that no scenario or phantom claim takes).
reconciliation-totals-reconciliation-lin: A Reconciliation line is one line of a Quality Check Reconciliation, with its own outcome: each Evidence Observation it holds is one line, and its Evidence Obligation is one more when no Evidence Observation that ran answers it. A scenario with no Evidence Obligation, no Pending Item and no Evidence Observation still has one Quality Check Reconciliation, holding neither, and it is a single line. No line stands in for another: a scenario whose one Evidence Obligation two passing tests answer adds one to the Claim Reconciliation total and two to the Reconciliation line total.
reconciliation-totals-evidence-obligatio: An Evidence Obligation is the evidence a scenario asks for, by the tags it carries, to be met by Evidence Observations. A pending tag such as `@unitpending` defers the evidence of its kind of quality check, and a deferral tag such as `@wip` defers all of the scenario's: what a tag defers raises no Evidence Obligation and is a Pending Item instead, tallied after the table, apart from balanced and out-of-balance, when there is one. On a scenario that shares its `@SCN` code with another, no tag defers anything: it reads "Evidence Obligation's @SCN code is carried by another Scenario" at each kind of quality check it raises, or once when it raises none.
reconciliation-totals-evidence-observati: An Evidence Observation is one reported result of a test or a fitness function, attributed by the codes it cites: to the one scenario that carries its one code, to a phantom claim when no scenario carries its one code, and otherwise to the unnamed claim, because no one scenario can take it. One that never reached its assertions is broken: it was reported, but did not run to a result.
pending-tally: {pending} Pending Item(s) — deferred, tallied apart from balanced and out-of-balance.
evidence-observations-sum: {total} evidence observations = {onScenario} on scenarios + {onPhantomClaim} on cited scenario ids with no real scenario + {onUnnamedClaim} that no one scenario can take.

fitness-ci-step: {steps} step(s), each named on its fitness function's row of Claim Reconciliations.
runner-layer-names-none: no runner: the target declares this layer has none, by setting it to `null` under `specController.runners` in its `package.json`.
runner-layer-unnamed: unnamed: the target leaves this layer's runner undeclared: `specController.runners` in its `package.json` is missing or not a block, leaves the layer out, or gives it a value that is neither a string nor `null`. A string there names the layer's runner.
no-step-counted-as-its-runner-runs-it: no step counted as its runner runs it.
reconciler-reconciles: this step runs the reconciliation this report is
reconciler-records: this step writes the step record the reconciliation reads
step-non-check: {entry} — a non-check: the target names it under `specController.notChecks`.
step-accounting-table-header: | Workflow | Job | Steps read | Candidates | Runners | Reconciler | Non-checks | GitHub plumbing | Accounted for |
step-accounting-not-applied-workflows-re: Not applied, because each {key} entry below names a workflow this run did not read (this run read {workflows}):
step-accounting-not-applied-no-workflow-: Not applied, because each {key} entry below names a workflow this run did not read (this run read no workflow):
step-accounting-candidates-term: A Candidate is a step read that is not a Runner, Reconciler, Non-check or GitHub plumbing step. It is read as a fitness function, and no list below names it.
step-accounting-reconciler-term: A Reconciler step runs this reconciliation or writes the step record it reads.
step-accounting-non-checks-term: A Non-check is a step the target names under `specController.notChecks`, unless it is a Reconciler step. A GitHub plumbing step named there is a Non-check too.
step-accounting-plumbing-term: A GitHub plumbing step is one that is neither a Reconciler nor a Non-check step and uses one of GitHub's own actions `actions/checkout`, `actions/cache`, `actions/upload-artifact`, `actions/download-artifact` or `actions/setup-*`. A step that runs a command, an install included, is never plumbing.
step-accounting-accounted-for-term: Accounted for is the sum of the five columns from Candidates to GitHub plumbing, in which each step read is counted once.
scenario-claim-reconciliations-out-of-ba: {outOfBalance} of {claimReconciliations} Claim Reconciliation(s) of scenarios out of balance
not-grouped-by-feature: {ungrouped} out of balance, not grouped by feature (no feature file names them)
phantom-claim-reconciliations: {count} Claim Reconciliation(s) for cited scenario ids with no real scenario
unnamed-claim-reconciliations: {count} Claim Reconciliation(s) for evidence observations no one scenario can take
phantom-claim-tally: {count} Claim Reconciliation(s) for cited scenario ids with no real scenario.
unnamed-claim-tally: {count} Claim Reconciliation(s) for evidence observations no one scenario can take, aggregated into "{unnamedClaimId}".
excluded-scn-occurrences: {count} @SCN ids seen in non-tag context, excluded: each is an @SCN code written in a feature file's prose, a comment or step text rather than as a tag, so it marks no scenario and raises no claim
shared-scn-codes: The corpus holds {scenarios} scenarios — {codes} @SCN code(s) carried by more than one scenario, each scenario named as `feature file : scenario title`:
evidence-cell-key:
Key: each evidence cell reads *obligation*/*observations*.
- The letter says the scenario's tags raise an Evidence Obligation of that kind: (F)itness, (U)nit, (I)ntegration, (E)2e, (P)erformance. `-` means they raise none of that kind, as a pending tag raises none unless the scenario shares its `@SCN` code with another.
- The number counts the scenario's Evidence Observations of that kind that ran. `-` means none.
- For example, `U/2` is a unit obligation answered by two unit tests; `U/-` is a unit obligation that no unit test answered; `-/1` is one unit test citing a scenario that raises no unit obligation, which puts the row out of balance even where its unit evidence is pending.
- A blank cell means no obligation and no Evidence Observation that ran; `—` marks the row of a phantom claim or of the unnamed claim.
- A row named `feature file : scenario title` is a scenario that carries no @SCN code. The run reads none of its tags, so its evidence cells are blank, and its reconciling item says that no Evidence Observation can link to it.
- In Reconciling items, `—` means the row has no reconciling item, and *untagged* means a scenario that carries an @SCN code and no tag that raises an Evidence Obligation.
- On the unnamed claim's row, the counts after an item, such as `1 ran, 1 passed, 0 failed`, are of that item's own tests, and a fitness item counts its CI steps; a broken item stands alone, outside those counts.
- CI steps names the steps the Evidence observations table gives for each kind of quality check other than fitness that the row obligates or observes, whether or not an Evidence Observation of that kind ran for the row, and the step each of the row's fitness Evidence Observations names: `U/-` beside a step names the step that runs unit tests, none of which answered this row. A blank CI steps cell means no such step is known.
watermelon-item-key: - Where a row's item says its CI step or its job sets `continue-on-error`, the name in parentheses after it is its fitness function. Remove `continue-on-error` from its CI step and from its job, or set it to false, and the check's red fails the CI run.
check-step-no-outcome: {scnId}: the CI run's record carries no outcome for this check's step — so the check did not run.
check-step-skipped: {scnId}: the CI run's record says this check's step was skipped — so the check did not run.
check-step-ended: {scnId}: the CI run's record says this check's step ended `{outcome}` — so the check did not run.
ambiguous-named-step: The step "{step}" is ambiguous — two or more step definitions match it, so the step never ran.
ambiguous-unnamed-step: A step is ambiguous — two or more step definitions match it, so the step never ran.
outcome-satisfied: Evidence Observation satisfies its Evidence Obligation
outcome-watermelon: Evidence Observation is passing but its CI step or its job sets `continue-on-error` so its red might not fail the CI run
outcome-no-scn-code: Evidence Obligation has no @SCN code for an Evidence Observation to link to
outcome-duplicate-scn-code: Evidence Obligation's @SCN code is carried by another Scenario
outcome-cites-unknown-scenario: Evidence Observation cites an unknown Scenario
outcome-no-evidence-obligation: Evidence Observation cites a Scenario with no matching Evidence Obligation
outcome-broken: Evidence Observation is broken because its proof never ran to a result
outcome-both-missing: Evidence Obligation and Evidence Observation are both missing — the Scenario is untagged and uncited
several-scn-codes-cited: {count} scenario codes cite {codes} — a test cites exactly one scenario, so this one credits none of them.
shared-scn-code: {code} is carried by more than one scenario, so evidence citing it credits none of them.
evidence-obligation-diverges-from-outcom: QualityCheckReconciliation invariant (@SCN-LDG-030): outcome "{outcome}" has the evidence obligation (debit) side {presenceForOutcome} for that outcome, but it was {presenceFound}.
evidence-observation-diverges-from-outco: QualityCheckReconciliation invariant (@SCN-LDG-030): outcome "{outcome}" has the evidence observation side {presenceForOutcome} for that outcome, but it was {presenceFound}.
